description_full: Vibra Energia S.A. manufactures, processes, distributes, trades in, transports, imports, and exports oil-based products, lubricants, and other fuels. It operates in Gas Station Network, B2B, and Renewable segments. The company markets petroleum-derived fuels, lubricants, vehicular natural gas, biofuels, and convenience products. It also sells fuels and lubricants, and provides associated services to its consumer's market, as well as markets aviation products and services at Brazil's airport facilities. The company was incorporated in 1971 and is based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 3K people. Revenue per employee of $8.9M ranks in the top quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers. Each employee generates $244K of free cash flow annually.
financial_summary: Vibra Energia SA is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $6.4B market cap on $33.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 17% against a 9% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 5% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $924M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.37× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.0× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sector_headwinds.text: Low reinvestment-driven growth suggests the compounding engine has stalled
Fragmented industry with below-average profit capture — no moat to protect margins
Gross margin trails most Consumer Cyclical peers — competitors appear to have the pricing hand
Consumer demand is fundamentally cyclical — a recession compresses both unit volume and pricing power, and operating leverage cuts both ways.
E-commerce margin compression and tariff exposure — digital competition erodes pricing power while trade policy reshuffles supply-chain cost structures overnight.
Brand relevance decay — shifting consumer preferences and social-media-driven trends can strand inventory and invalidate positioning faster than product cycles can adapt.

Altman Z comfortably in the safe zone — a fortress balance sheet on this measure

own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 0%.
